small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs now that the (64,64,16) variant is known to compile: try `(BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=2)` and `(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=8, num_stages=3)`; with 4 accumulators of size BM×BN, BN=128/BM=128 reduces program count over N=128, OC=128, OUT_SPATIAL=3969.
- The 4 separate `tl.dot` calls reuse the same `w` tile but reload `x` with offset+1, +IW, +IW+1; instead load a single `(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N + 1 + IW)` style tile once or, simpler, load the 2×2 pool window as a `(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N*4)` x-tile and do one larger `tl.dot`, then reduce-max across the 4 lanes — fewer dot ops, better tensor-core utilization.
- Swap program axes so `pid_sp` is axis 0 (largest) to improve L2 reuse of weights across the OC tiles within an N, and consider grouping N into the OC axis (`pid = n*OC_tiles + oc_tile`) to keep SM occupancy high.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a pool-fused im2col GEMM where each program computes a `BLOCK_M (OC) × BLOCK_N (pooled positions)` tile but expands K to include the 2×2 pool window (i.e. K = IC·KH·KW·4 in a virtual sense). Concretely, gather the 4×4 input footprint per pooled position and run a single tensor-core GEMM producing 4 conv outputs that are immediately max-reduced, instead of 4 separate `tl.dot`s. This halves index math and improves MMA pipelining.
- Switch to channels-last (NHWC) input layout and lay weights as (KH·KW·IC, OC) so the GEMM-K dim is contiguous in memory; current NCHW gather forces strided IH·IW reads per channel inside the K loop. Pre-permute once in `__init__` for weights, and permute the input in `forward` (or accept NHWC).
- Consider a persistent-kernel design with one program per (N, OC tile) sweeping over all pooled spatial tiles, so the weight tile is loaded once per OC block and reused across the whole feature map — weight reuse is the dominant bandwidth term at OC=128, K=576.
